key_points: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled, rising from a ~600/month baseline (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180 in August and 1260 in September 2026 (E-04).

Disputed bills split 59% ACTUAL read type (1785) and 41% ESTIMATED read type (1240) (E-01); the initial request (CL-01, SH-CS) framed this as a response-handling problem, but ticket response times were within SLA (E-03), so that hypothesis was rejected.

Of the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills, 1184 (95%) had a valid, timely AMI read that was exported to billing but rejected at import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, not a missing/lost read (E-12); this invalidated the earlier hypothesis that field-reader staffing shortfalls (E-05, E-07) caused these disputes.

The rejection mechanism was traced to validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares the raw cumulative register value against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-13), combined with meter firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) recording registers in 0.1 m3 units versus legacy m3 (E-14) - a 10x mismatch that systematically misflags normal usage as high-consumption.

Billing-db and mdms-export independently and consistently identify the same 1184 affected accounts, cross-confirming the mechanism and the integrity of the MDMS-to-billing handoff H-MDMS-BILL (E-15, E-16, E-17).

The committed release scope is limited to verify_handoff_integrity:H-MDMS-BILL (SD-2), which was completed (work item W-WI-HANDOFF-VERIFY-MDMS-BILL, DONE); broader remedies such as patching BV-17 or re-billing affected accounts were not executed.

The cause of the ACTUAL-read majority of disputes (59%, 1785 bills) remains unattributed and unresolved (VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE, open), as the BV-17 estimate-substitution mechanism only explains the ESTIMATED-read cohort.
No automated writes to customer bills occurred and no unconfirmed field-dispatch changes were made, consistent with the authority constraints K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH recorded in the input.

proposal.summary: The problem (PD-1@v2) was defined as CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubling from a ~600/month baseline (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep 2026) (E-04), with disputed bills splitting 59% ACTUAL (1785) / 41% ESTIMATED (1240) read type (E-01). Investigation found that 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills (95%) had a valid, timely AMI read that was rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rather than missing (E-12), traced to validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-13) failing to apply correct unit scaling for v4.2 meter firmware, which records registers in 0.1 m3 units versus legacy m3 (E-14) - a 10x mismatch. This superseded the initial requester framing (response-handling automation gap, CL-01/SH-CS, rejected by E-03) and the earlier hypothesis that field-reader staffing shortages (E-05, E-07) caused the ESTIMATED-read disputes (contradicted by E-12). Billing-db and mdms-export independently agree on the same 1184 affected accounts (E-15, E-16, E-17), confirming the MDMS-to-billing handoff (H-MDMS-BILL) is intact and that this is a billing-import rule defect, not a data-delivery failure. The committed release scope (SD-2) was limited to verifying this handoff integrity, which was completed. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with no holds, because the DEFINE Gate reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS and several verification obligations (notably on the ACTUAL-read dispute cause and BV-17's current status) remain open but lie outside the committed release scope. The BV-17 patch itself was not applied, no automated bill writes occurred (consistent with K-BILLWRITE), and no unconfirmed dispatch changes were made (consistent with K-DISPATCH).
